1.name: Pot body
1.note: The vessel that holds the water and food, and the pressure acting on the lid.

2.name: Base capsule
2.note: A magnetic steel skin on the underside, so the pot works on induction hobs. It also encloses the heat disc.

3.name: Heat disc
3.note: Spreads the hob's heat across the pot floor so the water boils evenly.

4.name: Lid
4.note: Closes the pot with six bayonet lugs. The pressure under it pushes up on the whole Ø220 gasket circle.

5.name: Gasket
5.note: The seal between lid and pot. Steam pressure presses its lip harder against the wall, so it seals better as the pressure rises.

6.name: Main handle
6.note: The long handle on the pot. Phenolic stays cool to the touch.

7.name: Handle bracket
7.note: Welded to the pot wall to carry a handle.

8.name: Helper handle
8.note: The short handle on the opposite side, so you can lift the pot with two hands.

9.name: Lid handle
9.note: The handle you turn to engage or release the bayonet lugs. It also houses the lock slide and its spring.

10.name: Pan screw
10.note: Fixes a handle to its bracket.

11.name: Valve stem
11.note: The vent pipe through the lid. Its Ø3 bore is the orifice the operating weight sits on.

12.name: Thin nut
12.note: Clamp the valve stem to the lid, one on each side.

13.name: Operating weight
13.note: Sits on the stem and lifts to vent steam. Its weight over the Ø3 bore sets the pressure, 86 kPa gauge, and so the 118 °C boiling point.

14.name: Seal washer
14.note: Seals the valve stem against the lid, inside and out.

15.name: Lock pin
15.note: The interlock. Pressure lifts it at 3 kPa, so it blocks the lid slide and seals its own vent. It drops again below 1.5 kPa.

16.name: O-ring
16.note: Seals the lock pin in its bore. Its drag is part of what the pin must overcome to rise.

17.name: Lock slide
17.note: Slides under the lid handle to hold the lid turned shut. With the pin up it cannot move, so the lid cannot be turned.

18.name: Slide spring
18.note: Pushes the lock slide back to its locked position.

19.name: Safety valve body
19.note: The housing of the back-up valve, for when the main vent is blocked.

20.name: Safety plunger
20.note: Held on its seat by the safety spring. If the pressure passes 160 kPa gauge it lifts and vents the pot.

21.name: Safety seal
21.note: The soft face on the safety plunger that seals the Ø3 seat until the valve opens.

22.name: Safety spring
22.note: Sets the safety valve's opening pressure by holding the plunger down.

23.name: Button screw
23.note: Fixes the lid handle to the lid from underneath.

24.name: Slide knob
24.note: The grip on the lock slide, for sliding it by hand.
